evidence.root_reported_execution: One actual separate offline interpretation, exit 0; no original workload replay.

scope: Independent reading and arithmetic over the completed derived report, plus exact R24 profile source review. No target program/parser/auditor, host API, Cargo, workload or runtime mutation.
findings: Both ON rounds rank the same two validation scopes first. Their combined share is about 61% of measured controller CPU in each round, although absolute CPU/call differs substantially between rounds.

These scopes enclose complete validation, including fresh path/inode checks, full content reads, reference comparison or ring SHA256, cancellation/deadline checks, and policy/shell checks. D1 does not split those internal costs; the measured 14.0137 ms/call is not a pure hashing measurement.
The owner scope also performs verify_boundaries after the second complete verify_files_checked. Its additional work cannot be assumed to be only scheduling or hashing.

The reference implementation already uses ring for SHA256 and retains bounded exact reference bytes for fixed public executables. Its 2 MiB budget is allocated to SSH first, then false, then shell; a non-fitting file leaves the remaining budget unchanged. The historical 156720-byte figure alone does not establish what this campaign retained.

Router construction is only about 2.57% of measured controller CPU here and follows the already tried R30 direction. The prior R33 path work and R35 allocation/command changes are also not new candidates merely because a related coarse scope is visible.

Spawn and process-identity observations are material enough to retain as measurements, but the current trace does not identify a specific low-risk redundant operation that can be removed while preserving original generation ownership, waits and cleanup.
The data justify a narrower validation diagnostic, not a new production optimization patch or adoption decision. They do not establish that R24 is globally optimal.

selected_d2_preimplementation_direction.selected_by_root: Three file segments plus method-level boundary/shell/policy; diagnostic feature only.
phases: The one unchanged complete content loop, labeled reference-compare versus ring-hash according to existing immutable reference state
selected_d2_preimplementation_direction.required_semantics: Original full passes, 16 KiB checks, short-circuit/error order, cancellation/deadline and lifetime-owner closure remain unchanged. Read-loop labels describe combined read+compare/hash+guard cost, not pure read or hash.
selected_d2_preimplementation_direction.cost_accounting: After child spans are added, validation parent inclusive CPU is the complete validation total; parent exclusive CPU is the residual. Never add parent inclusive to child CPU.
selected_d2_preimplementation_direction.predicted_frozen_fixture_events: Approximately 361 events/request and 80142 events for a 222-request first controller; this is a static estimate, not an executed result.

limitations: This finite C1 diagnostic does not establish C8/C16 throughput or cancellation/lifecycle behavior.
OFF/ON differences and the large round variation are not optimization benefit or statistical significance.
Signed uninstrumented/counter-window residuals remain signed and are not assigned to SSH, remote CPU or network.
A zero CPU-event count means no synchronous CPU observation for that phase, not zero real work.
The original parent/adapter remain failed; the separate successful analysis does not rewrite their result.
